proposedControllingInterpretation.countingUnit: Distinct canonical IDs of all current material defects in the existing Stage14 scope.
proposedControllingInterpretation.membership: Include each such defect until one current admissibly established, evidence-supported RCA establishes its known cause at the earliest defective layer required by the existing Stage14 contract.
proposedControllingInterpretation.unestablishedCases: An absent RCA, a stale/rejected/inadmissible RCA, semantic-UNKNOWN cause content or other missing required affirmative support does not remove the defect from this population. Contradictory sufficient evidence follows the existing contradiction/UNKNOWN gates; do not choose a favorable RCA to clear the defect.
proposedControllingInterpretation.relationshipToBlockedAnalyses: Overlap with BLOCKED_ANALYSES is permitted. No disjoint partition, complement equation or replacement of that independent field is implied.
proposedControllingInterpretation.records: Do not fabricate RCA records or accepted UNKNOWN review records to represent missing analysis. Derive the projection from the preserved current material-defect population and its actual current RCA/evidence relationships.
proposedControllingInterpretation.preservedRequirements: Every current material defect still requires the original evidence-supported RCA; unknown RCA remains blocked. Existing author/application authority, currentness, evidence, review and F2 input-basis duties remain. No new RCA authoring family, writer or operation is added.

rationale: Existing-RCA-only counting can yield zero when one current material defect has no RCA. Although a separate completion blocker can prevent favorable acceptance, that projection omits the unresolved material defect from the field named UNDETERMINED_ROOT_CAUSES. The selected defect-based population keeps missing analyses visible and aligns this summary with the explicit every-current-material-defect RCA duty without inventing records or shrinking its universe. This is an explicit narrow choice among previously source-compatible populations, not a retroactive assertion that the old source uniquely chose it.

16.2 Canonical-family sole-authority rule

Canonical record families are the sole substantive authority for canonical project data. Stage-data fields that correspond to canonical records may contain only: (a) pre-acceptance proposal payloads, (b) immutable canonical ID references, or (c) application-recomputed summaries. Duplicated substantive canonical values in stage data are prohibited. Any summary/reference mismatch fails integrity validation and cannot be resolved by choosing whichever copy is convenient.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

34.3 Registered normalizers and derivations

Every normalizer and application derivation has an immutable registry ID, version, implementation-owner file, canonical input contract, output contract, hash or build identity, and invalidation consequences. Every derived value records the exact derivation ID and source-record hashes. A changed normalizer or derivation invalidates affected current values and results unless an explicit compatibility migration proves byte- and semantic-equivalent output.

Every release-bearing derivation and normalizer is completely defined by this specification or by an explicitly named versioned normative algorithm. The semantics defined in Sections 14.6, 15, 16.1, 26, 29, 30, 31, 34.1, 34.2, and 36 control their registry entries, and an entry cannot deviate from them. A release-bearing derivation or normalizer whose semantics are not so defined is UNDEFINED_DERIVATION and blocks acceptance.
